feature: Q and W trim the clip under the playhead up to it
summary: Park the playhead where the good part starts and press Q, or where it ends and press W: the piece under the playhead loses everything up to (or after) the playhead and the gap closes on every track, in one key instead of a cut, a click and a Delete.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording; the timeline has the keyboard as soon as it opens.

try.do: Open the sample recording and drag the playhead to two seconds.
Press Command Z, and check the two seconds come back in one step.
Put the playhead at five seconds and press W.
Undo, park the playhead inside the clip, right-click the clip and choose Ripple Trim Start to Playhead.
Split a clip with Command K, park inside the second piece and press Q: only that piece loses its head.
Click the canvas and press W: it picks the Magic Wand, not a trim.

evaluate: After Q, is it right that the playhead jumps to the new first frame of the piece, the way Premiere does?
Should Q and W also cut music on another track that runs under the trimmed stretch (they do now, to keep everything in sync), or leave the music alone?
Are Ripple Trim Start to Playhead and Ripple Trim End to Playhead the right names, or would Premiere's Previous Edit and Next Edit read better to you?
Is it clear enough that Q and W only mean trim while the timeline has the keyboard?
rough: No mock draws Q and W or the clip's right-click menu; the nearest, the video page's overflow menu, only has Split at playhead. The rows follow Premiere's names and sit right under Split at Playhead.
The clip's right-click menu opens at the foot of the screen and now scrolls sooner: in the capture only its first three rows show before the scroll arrow. The ruler menu already had this problem.
Q and W act on the piece under the playhead, not on the piece you right-clicked, so the menu rows go dim on any piece the playhead is not in.
In the walk, the Command Z step runs through the harness's undo action, because a walk's menu bar is frozen. Undo was not pressed on the real key.
